title: Police shoot murder suspect
article: A 34-year-old man suspected of stabbing two women, including one fatally, was shot to death during a confrontation with a police officer in a North York home.

The province's Special Investigations Unit is probing the circumstances surrounding the shooting, while investigators from Toronto Police's homicide squad and 31 Division are investigating the stabbings.

According to police, officers responded to a disturbance call at a townhouse at 1898 Sheppard Ave. W. near Jane Street shortly after 11 p.m. Friday. They located 37-year-old Marcia Whyte with serious stab wounds on a walkway outside the townhouse. Inside, officers found 62-year-old Pandora Whyte, who was later pronounced dead at the scene.

The SIU said a man inside the home was shot after a confrontation with an officer. The wounded man, Ucal Lauzon, was taken to Sunnybrook and Women's College Health Sciences Centre where he died at around 3 a.m. Saturday.
Marcia was taken to the same hospital where she underwent emergency surgery.

An autopsy revealed Pandora died of "multiple sharp force injuries." Pandora lived in the townhouse where she was killed. SIU spokesperson Rose Bliss wouldn't disclose how many times or where in the body Lauzon was shot.
